method: Saved evidence and source review only; no benchmark rerun or sample modification
findings: Both C++ modes call the same predict lambda and ExactKnnClassifier::predict_optimized once per sample. There is no alternate model, cached prediction path, extra search in the resident timer, or different native build in saved evidence.

Resident internal timer surrounds full query validation, exact search, vote and score/label allocation. Hashing and IPC follow timer stop. Fresh internal timer has the same scope; fresh outer timer additionally includes process startup, CSV loading, fit, serialization and exit.
Fresh C++ outer time exceeds its own internal prediction by about 0.37 seconds, confirming that scope accounting is consistent. Persistent process prediction itself is slower in this session.
Resident C++ samples are consistently about 3.68 seconds and fresh internal samples about 1.77 seconds. This is a phase/process-mode regime difference, not an outlier-driven median.

All resident workers and Python models coexist during the resident phase; native workers are closed before the later fresh-process block. Process residency, scheduler placement and memory/cache state therefore differ between scopes.

Observed affinity permitted all 20 logical CPUs. Executed core placement, clock frequency, temperature, paging and background JVM activity were not sampled. Scheduling, cache/memory or frequency explanations remain hypotheses; the saved evidence does not identify a cause.
limitations: The two phases were measured in separate chronological blocks, with 20 resident trials and five fresh-process trials. Cross-phase medians are not matched observations of the same machine state.
Do not subtract medians across phases to infer startup overhead, claim that fresh execution inherently accelerates the kernel, or generalize these times to other machines/process placement.
Keep both scopes and every original sample. Main implementation ratios use the declared resident scope and matched final-workload trials; fresh pipeline evidence is a separate scope.
